info.title: No standard
info.text: There is no official pseudocode. Every exam board and textbook has its own, which is why OCR publishes a reference guide.

info.title: Close to Python
info.text: The reference language looks like Python on purpose, because so many schools teach Python, but the endif and next keywords are not Python.

info.title: Zero indexing
info.text: Arrays start at zero in most languages, a habit that comes from the arithmetic of memory addresses.

info.title: Off by one
info.text: The commonest loop bug in the world is running one time too many or too few. Count the repeats by hand when checking.

info.title: Write what you know
info.text: Examiners accept any clear language. Answering in the one you actually use is almost always safer.

info.title: Comments
info.text: Two slashes start a comment in the reference language. Comments are for people; the computer skips them.
